findings.reason: the untested half of the rule's predicate is the ordinary crashed-worker state, and without that case the guard can be widened to every stopped peer and still read green.
findings.text: §23's done-when never tests a peer whose process has ended but whose manifest is not terminal, so an implementation that keys the exemption on "the process has ended" alone passes every stated case

findings.reason: without the caller named and its module in scope, the node either stops for a scope extension mid-fix or keys the exemption on a remanent pointer field, and applying the rule unconditionally inside `_raise_repository_scope_conflict` would also release claims at dispatch, which `claim_disposition`'s own docstring measures as protecting work in five of six stopped claims.
findings.text: §23's reproduced D12 message is produced on the landing path only by `widen_claim(..., acceptance=True)` (`reckon/crew/claims.py:63`) calling `refuse_widen_scope_conflicts` and then `_raise_repository_scope_conflict` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:1578`), the shared function every dispatch claim check also uses; §23 names neither that caller nor `reckon/crew/claims.py` in its write paths, and the only acceptance marker already on the pointer (`accepted_scope_before_widening`) is set once and persists across later plain `crew widen` calls

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_accepted_scope_exceptions` with its `cannot accept <path>: live run <peer> claims <claim>` text, the `ScopeConflict` D12 wording, and `claim_disposition`'s `N commit(s) beyond its base that main cannot reach` reason all resolve and read as quoted in `reckon/crew/promotion_scope.py`, `reckon/crew/node.py` and `reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §23's cases cover a stopped completed peer (exemption applies), a live peer (refused as today) and a negative control, but there is no case for a peer whose process has ended while its manifest is not terminal, which is the other half of the rule's own predicate.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §23's gate lives in a temporary crew home, its logs are under the run directory, and its new test is a repository path; nothing is placed on node-local scratch.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names or ticket numbers reach §23's symbols, paths or comments.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the refusal §23 reproduces is raised only through `widen_claim(..., acceptance=True)` in `reckon/crew/claims.py`, which §23 neither names nor lists among its write paths, and the function it reaches there is the same one every dispatch claim check uses.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §23 carries one mechanism (the acceptance exemption for a stopped, terminal peer) and one done-when for it.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §23 declares no depends-on, and its two write paths (`reckon/crew/promotion_scope.py`, `reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py`) are listed by no other section, so nothing needs to sequence it; the cited plan slugs `the-monitor-shows-the-work-it-watches` and `a-coordinator-can-clear-its-own-duties`, and the evidence archive path `docs/evidence/archive/the-crew-does-its-own-bookkeeping-landed.html`, all resolve.
